absent: Layout of e820 table and entry structures and behavior of range add and type print helpers.
Implementation of real_trim_memory, x86_get_mtrr_mem_range, range buffers, and cleanup control flags.
Definitions of mtrr_if dispatch, num_var_ranges, usage table, mtrr mutex, and low level set_mtrr path.
MSR numbers, register bit layouts, capability bits, and CPU model constants beyond names seen.
Effective type precedence and compatibility rules used when merging or comparing memory types.
Callers, ordering, and locking context for trim, copy, rebuild, save, and file operations.

findings.text: Init wrapper retypes an address interval in the global firmware memory table and reports how many bytes were actually retyped, delegating all overlap handling to the table helper.

Range update requires distinct old and new types and treats identical types as a fatal programming error, clamps a size that would overflow the address maximum, emits a debug log of the interval and type transition, and returns the total retyped length.

For each entry of the requested old type the updater applies three cases in order: fully covered entries are retyped in place, entries enclosing the request are split into retained head plus new middle plus retained tail, and partial overlaps add a new slice for the intersection then shrink or shift the old entry to the leftover head or tail.

Boot time trim scans variable MTRRs, builds the covered physical ranges including an optional top of memory extension, removes head gap and holes and top beyond coverage from the memory map, warns about lost megabytes when trimming occurred, and returns one on trim else zero.

Trimming runs only when MTRRs are enabled, the CPU advertises the feature, trimming is not disabled, and the default type is uncachable; it aborts on blank virtualized tables, on missing writeback entries, and when populated types contain anything beyond writeback and uncachable.
Fixed block descriptor holds a base MSR identifier and a count of subranges in that block; the static table describes one 64K block, two 16K blocks, and eight 4K blocks, terminated by an empty entry.
Lookup map entry holds inclusive start and exclusive end addresses, flags, an eight bit memory type, and a one bit fixed marker distinguishing fixed from variable coverage.
Maximum lookup entries equals the fixed range count plus twice the maximum variable range count, allowing each variable range to split at most one existing interval.

Diagnostic line width is eighty characters; type names map zero to uncachable, one to write-combining, four to write-through, five to write-protect, six to write-back, with placeholders for indices two and three.

Both Cyrix and generic operation tables expose variable register count where applicable plus get, set, free region search, page validation, and write-combining support callbacks; Cyrix advertises eight variable registers.

Cyrix read disables interrupts, enables address range register mapping through the control register, fetches three base bytes and a region control byte, restores mapping and interrupts, then derives page frame base, power of two size with 4K granularity on low registers and 256K on register seven, and type from distinct control value maps for the two groups.

Cyrix allocator honors any explicitly requested register, prefers register seven immediately for requests above 32M, otherwise scans low registers for an empty slot before falling back to register seven when the request is at least 256K, and reports no space when no candidate is empty.

Cyrix register reads and generic variable register programming run with interrupts saved and restored around the hardware access; programming additionally disables and reenables caches around the register writes.

Cyrix programming prologue saves CR4 and clears page global enable when present, sets cache disable with writeback invalidates around it, and saves then enables control mapping; epilogue flushes again, restores control, clears cache disable, and restores CR4 when page global enable was present.

Cyrix write scales sizes for register seven, masks to fifteen bits, encodes the position of the highest set bit as the hardware size field, translates generic memory types to distinct control codes for low versus high registers, shifts the base to bytes, and programs the three address bytes plus control code between the cache control prologue and epilogue.

Type lookup folds a half open interval over the ordered map, merging default type for leading gaps and for trailing past the last entry, merging each overlapping entry and advancing the cursor to its end, returning uncachable when state was never set or the feature is disabled, and reporting whether the whole interval shared one type.

Merge treats invalid as identity returning the new type, otherwise combines old and new through effective type precedence and clears the uniformity flag whenever the combination differs from the accumulated type.

One shot guest override is accepted only before boot processor init, only under a hypervisor, and only on specific confidential or paravirtual platforms; it clears the MTRR capability to freeze later changes, copies at most the maximum variable entries, records default type and enabled state, and latches the set flag, warning and truncating on oversized input.

Init copy queries the required map size, leaves the map null when disabled or empty, otherwise allocates under the MTRR mutex, copies the early table and records the new capacity, and disables MTRRs with an error when allocation fails.

Rebuild is a no-op unless the generic backend is active, otherwise it resets the entry count to the fixed prefix and re-adds variable coverage; fixed save copies fixed hardware state into the saved state only when fixed ranges exist.

Identical old and new types trap as a programming error; inconsistent fixed, variable, or default type state across CPUs emits warnings and a BIOS advisory; a BIOS supplied variable mask with non-canonical high bits is repaired and taints the kernel for firmware workaround.

Validation rejects unaligned or non power of two aligned requests by shifting base and last until parity diverges and comparing; on early Pentium Pro steppings it additionally requires 4M base alignment and forbids writable types in a specific low window that may hang the CPU.

Map copy and region add serialize on the MTRR mutex; region add additionally holds the CPU hotplug read lock across search and program so the CPU set cannot change, and variable read pins the current CPU across MSR accesses.

Region add validates alignment, type range, write-combining support, non-zero size, and physical width, then under locks scans for overlap: enclosing same type marks for replacement and compatible types are skipped, partial or mismatched overlaps fail, enclosed same type bumps usage and returns, otherwise it allocates a free slot, programs it, migrates usage on replacement and clears the old slot.

File based add lazily allocates a per file per register use count sized by variable register count, requires page alignment and converts to page frames when the caller passes bytes, delegates to page add with increment, and bumps the file count for the allocated register.
Generic allocator accepts a caller supplied replacement index inside range immediately, otherwise returns the first variable register whose size reads zero, and reports no space when all are in use.

Generic read returns zero base size and type for entries whose mask valid bit is clear; otherwise it reconstructs base and size from base and masked address bits with reserved high bits excluded, expands the mask to all ones above its highest set bit, and derives type from the low base bits.

Generic write clears the mask register and saved state for zero size to disable, otherwise composes base and mask low and high halves from page frame values with type and valid bits and reserved high bits excluded, writes base then mask, and mirrors the values into saved variable state.

Early map storage is a fixed capacity init array referenced by a mutable pointer with refdata lifetime, with size, used count, and fixed prefix count; module globals track SMP inconsistency mask, one shot state latch, top of memory extension, saved MTRR state, last fixed window, default type halves, reserved high bits, and a debug flag set only by the debug boot parameter.
Generic write-combining probe reads the capability MSR and tests its write-combining bit, while the positive variant unconditionally reports support for hardware that always allows it.
